user: I'm CUS-0004. Transaction TX-0401, 240.00 EUR: the goods never arrived. Which reason code applies? State the transaction ID and amount too. Do not open a dispute.
answer:
What I did
- I retrieved your account and the transaction list for ACC-1005 and searched our dispute rules.

What I found
- Transaction ID: TX-0401
- Amount: 240.00 EUR
- Merchant: TechMart Online
- Date: 2026-07-20
- Status: settled

Applicable reason code
- The correct reason code for "goods never arrived" is goods_not_received.

Eligibility note (important)
- Our dispute rules show goods_not_received has a 90-day window from the transaction date. TX-0401 is dated 2026-07-20, which places it outside that 90-day window, so it is not eligible for dispute under that reason code.

What happens next
- Per your instruction, I will not open a dispute. If you’d like, I can:
  - Attempt a formal eligibility check (I would run check_dispute_eligibility) and report the result, or
  - Escalate this to a human agent to review possible next steps, or
  - Provide a statement or guidance on contacting the merchant.

Tell me which of those you want me to do next.

Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each reason code has a window in days from the transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Dispute handling process
## Review timelines
The review target is 10 business days for card reason codes and 20 business
days for transfer reason codes. Complex cases involving a foreign acquirer may
run to 45 calendar days; the customer is notified when that happens.

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.

Notifications
## Dispute updates
A dispute generates a notification on every state change. The notification
names the state, never the internal reason for a decision.
